name: Tiger Iron
physical: Traditionally linked to stamina and endurance
Often carried by athletes and manual workers
summary: Tiger Iron is the banded mix of golden tiger's eye, red jasper and black hematite, a powerful stone for stamina, grounding and steady willpower.
intro: Tiger iron is a striking metamorphic rock combining bands of golden-brown tiger's eye, red jasper and shimmering silver-black hematite. The three components give it a glittering, striped look that seems to flash in the light. It is mined mainly in Western Australia and in South Africa. Because it mixes fibrous quartz with iron minerals, tiger iron is heavy and tough, though the hematite layers can rust if left wet. Often sold as cabochons, beads, spheres and palm stones, it is popular for pieces that need a bold, masculine look and the energy that goes with it.
history: Tiger iron comes from banded iron formations in ancient rocks, particularly in the Pilbara region of Western Australia, where such rocks formed more than two billion years ago. It was cut for ornamental use only in the twentieth century. Other names such as Mary Ellen jasper recall a Minnesota location, though that is a different rock. The mixture of tiger's eye, jasper and hematite arises from alteration of crocidolite-bearing iron formations. Rockhounds love it for its heavy, glittering look and for the way it polishes into dramatic patterns. Because many cutters prefer easy materials, tiger iron is moderately priced, and it has become a standard crystal shop item.
meaning: Tiger iron is the stone of strength and stamina in crystal tradition. Healers connect it to the root, sacral and solar plexus chakras and say it brings together the confidence of tiger's eye, the grounding of red jasper and the shielding of hematite. It is used by people who need to push through tiring work or hold their ground under pressure. Many practitioners believe it gives a steady, enduring kind of energy rather than a quick burst. It is also linked to practical courage, setting boundaries and acting on plans. Because its energy is strong, some people prefer to keep it away from their bedside. Think of it as a stone of rugged determination.
howToUse: Carry a tiger iron palm stone or pocket piece when you need endurance, whether for training, long drives or demanding days. Wear it as a bracelet for steady contact. Place a polished piece on your desk to support perseverance with projects. Hold it in meditation near the base of the spine and imagine energy rising slowly. Pair it with black tourmaline for protection or clear quartz to clarify goals. Avoid long water exposure, since the hematite layers may tarnish.
care: Tiger iron contains hematite, so avoid water soaks, which may cause rusting or dulling. Wipe it with a dry or barely damp cloth and dry it right away. Cleanse by smoke, sound, moonlight or selenite. It tolerates sun. Store it in a dry place, apart from harder gems, and avoid ultrasonic cleaners and acids. Oils from skin can be wiped off with a soft cloth.
identify: Real tiger iron shows distinct bands of golden fibrous tiger's eye, red jasper and metallic hematite in the same piece, and it feels heavy. Fakes include resin-bonded blends, dyed stones or painted patterns that lack the sparkle and weight of the real thing. Look for the shimmer of tiger's eye bands and the metallic gleam of hematite. A magnet may weakly attract the iron-bearing parts. If it feels light, it may be imitation.

faq.q: What is tiger iron made of?
faq.a: Tiger iron is a rock made of three components: golden tiger's eye, red jasper and metallic hematite. These form together in banded iron formations, giving the stone its striped, glittering look.

faq.q: What is tiger iron used for?
faq.a: Crystal healers use it for stamina, willpower and grounding. It is linked to the root, sacral and solar plexus chakras and is popular with people who want extra drive and a feeling of steady strength.

faq.q: Can tiger iron go in water?
faq.a: Avoid soaking it. The hematite and iron-bearing parts can dull or rust when wet for long. Wipe it with a barely damp cloth, dry it immediately and cleanse it with smoke, sound or moonlight instead.
